clue.text: Expect garden tool needs power input

parts.note: surface padding: the tool requires what follows

explanation.surface: A gardener's hoe that won't work without an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: "Expect" looks like a demand on the tool; it is the definition, standing apart from the gardening picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to look forward to something as likely is both to expect it and to anticipate it hopefully.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink drunk before dance

indicators.note: what comes before in time comes first in the answer, so the word for drunk leads

explanation.surface: Someone downs a cocktail before heading off to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: "Drunk" reads as a past participle about the drink; it is the adjective meaning intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: it names a spirit topped with soda and served over ice in a tall glass.

clue.text: Filling food getting father's thanks

explanation.surface: A child thanks Dad for a hearty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is informal British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: noodles and spaghetti are the classic stodgy, stomach-filling staple.

clue.text: Pitiable walkway — mention when returning

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word for mention is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sorry excuse for a footpath, worth remarking on during the trip back.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pitiable walkway" reads as one phrase; the dash splits the definition from the wordplay, and only the second word is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something that moves one to pity, or contemptibly poor.

clue.text: Place to live in settlement

explanation.surface: Looking for a home in a village or town.
explanation.walkthrough: "Settlement" suggests a village; here it means a compromise, as in two sides reaching an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers lodging and also a negotiated compromise between opposing parties.

clue.text: Loiter in E Sussex resort, second only to Brighton

indicators.note: second in order points at the letter in position two of Brighton

explanation.surface: Hanging about in a south-coast resort that always plays second fiddle to Brighton.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a town in East Sussex, England, joined to Brighton; "second only to" sounds like a ranking but just picks out one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to linger or hang about near one spot.

clue.text: Former magistrate new in war-torn Beirut

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the letter for new goes inside the rearranged city
a place torn apart by war is wrecked, so the letters of Beirut are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An ex-official arrives freshly in a Beirut devastated by conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: "War-torn" reads as plain description of the city, which is exactly why it hides so well as the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical sense: in ancient Rome this was an elected official who protected the plebeians, hence former.

clue.text: Signals for actor's lines to the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word for lines is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: An actor's prompts for delivering lines to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: "Lines" seems to be the actor's script; it is lines of people waiting. The 's stands for "is".
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre term: the words or actions that tell a performer when to speak or enter.

clue.text: Morning meal — some bananas about right?

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for some bananas wraps around the letter for right

explanation.surface: Is a few bananas the right thing for breakfast?
explanation.walkthrough: "Some" looks like it points to letters inside "bananas"; it asks for the word for a group of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of breakfast and lunch, eaten late in the morning.

clue.text: Audible prank after flatulence affecting the stomach

indicators.note: audible means able to be heard, so the prank is taken by its sound, not its spelling
the prank comes after, so it follows the word for flatulence

explanation.surface: A noisy practical joke following wind, with stomach trouble to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the two words together and the second is heard without its final K.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical adjective from the Greek for belly, used of anything to do with the stomach.

clue.text: Oscar limited by failing faculty of speech

indicators.note: something limited by a boundary is enclosed by it

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde, perhaps, hampered by a fading power of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: "Failing" looks like an adjective describing the faculty; it is a noun meaning a moral weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the human capacity to produce spoken sound.

clue.text: Mind supporter at home

explanation.surface: A request to look after a fan who's staying over.
explanation.walkthrough: "Mind" reads as a verb (look after); it is the noun. A supporter is an undergarment, not a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: the organ stands for the thinking self, as in 'use your head'.

clue.text: Babble, having knocked back strange spirit

indicators.note: to knock something back is to send it the other way, so both words are turned round

explanation.surface: Someone talks nonsense after downing an odd spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: "Knocked back" suggests drinking; it turns words round. Rum is British slang for strange, so one word is clued twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a low, continuous, indistinct sound of voices.

clue.text: Refreshment provided by Times press office

indicators.note: what is provided by something comes from it, so the letters are supplied by the words that follow

explanation.surface: Coffee laid on by a newspaper's press office.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across all three words, from the end of the first to the start of the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small strong coffee is one kind of refreshment.

clue.text: Hideous quality of arranged lessons at home

indicators.note: things arranged are set out in a new order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Home-schooling that has turned out rather ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: "At home" looks like the IN of many clues; here its letters are fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the state of being repellent or disgusting.

clue.text: Startled nearly everyone with a weapon

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word for everyone loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Almost everybody panics when someone produces a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's gun makes a fitting cause for the fright the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: suddenly frightened or disturbed.

clue.text: Avoid breaking peace around centre of armistice

indicators.note: something breaking falls to pieces, so the letters of peace are broken and reassembled
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters surround the middle letter
the centre of a word is its middle, so take the letter at the midpoint of armistice

explanation.surface: Steering clear of breaking the peace during a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: ARMISTICE has nine letters, so its fifth is the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to elude or get away from something, as in avoiding notice.

clue.text: Thirty-one days inside a yacht harbour

explanation.surface: A month spent aboard at a sailing port.
explanation.walkthrough: "Inside" looks like it puts one thing in another; it just supplies two letters. Thirty-one days is a month, here March.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a purpose-built dock where pleasure boats moor.

clue.text: I had the last of many lines for poem

indicators.note: the last of a series is its final member, so take the final letter of many

explanation.surface: A poet has had quite enough lines.
explanation.walkthrough: L is line, so doubling it gives lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a short pastoral poem describing rustic life.

clue.text: Easy to understand cold Shakespearean king

explanation.surface: A remark about how accessible a frosty Shakespeare monarch is.
explanation.walkthrough: C for cold, as on a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lucid, with no ambiguity.

clue.text: Manage over hard period

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so in a down clue the word for manage is read upwards

explanation.surface: Getting through a difficult stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard is the pencil grading.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a distinct era or age in history.

clue.text: Island is providing refuge for black bird

indicators.note: giving refuge means sheltering someone within

explanation.surface: An island offers sanctuary to a blackbird.
explanation.walkthrough: "Black bird" looks like one thing; black is a single letter and bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Not even make payment to get round politician

indicators.note: to get round something is to go about it, so the purchase word surrounds the politician

parts.note: to buy is to pay for something

explanation.surface: Not even paying off a politician will bring them round.
explanation.walkthrough: "Not even" reads as an emphatic opener; it is the definition, meaning uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an uneven surface full of lumps and jolts.

clue.text: Wicked devil promises to pay money back

explanation.surface: A rogue scribbles debt notes he never means to honour.
explanation.walkthrough: "Back" does not reverse anything; paying money back is what such notes promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: lacking reverence for God, hence sinful.

clue.text: Limit on court is party policy

explanation.surface: A statement that a legal limit is the party's policy.
explanation.walkthrough: "Court" suggests law; it is a tennis or basketball court.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports term: the boundary marking along each long edge of a playing area.

clue.text: Go away, taking time off from branch

indicators.note: taking time off means removing it, so the letter for time is removed
off from means away from, so the letter comes away from the word for branch

parts.note: a new shoot on a plant

explanation.surface: Someone told to clear off takes a break from a company branch.
explanation.walkthrough: "Branch" suggests an office; it is new growth on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection used to drive away animals or people, meaning be off.
